look_here_first: Robust upright pigweed with a reddish lower stem, obvious soft hairs on the upper stem and branches, and a short thick terminal green flower spike.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Amaranthaceae/Amaranthus: alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny unisexual flowers. Habit, plant sex, hairiness, nodal spines, cluster position, bract/tepal form, and fruit dehiscence are high-value characters.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: moderately to densely pubescent upper stem

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: short thick terminal and axillary inflorescences

lookalikes.differences: Hairiness is the fastest cue against smooth Palmer amaranth. It also lacks the paired nodal spines of A. spinosus.
